extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, PRSA members, ethics officers and chapter leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and advisory documents from the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA) on ethical standards, advisories, case studies, decision-making tools, and chapter-level best practices for public relations professionals. Focused on informing conduct, disclosure, reporting, and program development around PR ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Member Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Member Code of Ethics (Online) — includes an English and Spanish version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary statement of ethical principles and obligations for PRSA members; serves as the foundation for all advisories, case studies, and ethics programming. Contact information provided for questions (Judy Voss and Ethics Officers).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-7 (October 2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deceptive Practices by "Front" Groups and individuals using Blogs, Viral Marketing and anonymous Internet postings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory addressing deceptive representation and disclosure issues in online and viral communications, including use of anonymous postings and front groups; intended to guide acceptable practices and identify deceptive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-6 (April 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure by expert commentators and professional spokespersons of payment or financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on the obligation to disclose financial relationships or payments when providing expert commentary or acting as a professional spokesperson, to ensure transparency and avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-5 (January 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling the Truth, Especially in Wartime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses heightened ethical responsibilities around truthfulness during wartime or crisis situations; emphasizes accuracy and the ethical limits of messaging under extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-4 (August 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when and how PR professionals should report colleagues' or organizations' unethical or unprofessional conduct, including procedural and ethical considerations for filing reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-3 (July 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation of front groups with undisclosed sponsorships and/or deceptive or misleading descriptions of goals, causes, tactics, sponsors or participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against representing or participating in front groups that conceal sponsorship or misrepresent purposes; clarifies obligations to disclose sponsorship and avoid deceptive descriptions of campaigns or participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-2 (July 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overstating charges and/or compensation, financial or otherwise, for actual work performed by a public relations professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises against exaggerating fees, charges, or compensation relative to work performed; emphasizes honesty in billing and representations of services rendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS ADVISORY PS-1 (May 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of employment status of public relations agency staff or independent public relations consultants who work on-site at a client's offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clear disclosure of employment status when agency staff or consultants work on-site for clients so that roles and loyalties are transparent to stakeholders and publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilemmas and Moral Questions (document)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resource titled 'Dilemmas and Moral Questions' (downloadable PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material intended to present common ethical dilemmas faced by PR professionals; useful for training and for illustrating how the Code applies in real situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: An explanation about the PRSA Code of Ethics moving from Enforcement to Inspiration (document)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short explanatory paper about shifting the Code from an enforcement orientation toward inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the Code as aspirational guidance rather than solely punitive rules; useful context for interpreting ethical expectations and encouraging proactive ethical leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: A short guide to the process for ethical decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise guide describing a process for making ethical decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a stepwise decision-making approach practitioners can use when confronted with ethical choices (identify issue, stakeholders, options, consequences, alignment with Code, and choose/respond).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of the Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: Introductory material to a Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas (downloadable PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to use the matrix tool to analyze and categorize ethical problems, facilitating consistent evaluation and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: A downloadable 'Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas' tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical tool for mapping dilemmas, identifying relevant Code provisions, and guiding discussion or decision-making in workshops or ethics programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation about PRSA Member Code of Ethics 2000 (PowerPoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation materials (PowerPoint and PDF) on the PRSA Member Code of Ethics (2000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slide deck useful for training sessions and workshops to teach the Code's principles and application through examples and discussion prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Study #1 — Free Flow of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion key on the theme of Free Flow of Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a practical scenario and facilitator answers illustrating how the Free Flow of Information principle from the Code should be applied in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Study #2 — Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion key on Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates ethical issues around fair competition among practitioners, including examples and suggested discussion points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Study #3 — Disclosure of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion key on Disclosure of Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on disclosure obligations (e.g., sponsorship, payments, conflicts) with scenario-based analysis and recommended responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Study #4 — Safeguarding Confidences
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion key on Safeguarding Confidences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores obligations to protect confidential client information and the ethical boundaries for disclosure in varied contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Study #5 — Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion key on Conflicts of Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines examples of potential conflicts, disclosure requirements, and how to resolve or avoid conflicts consistent with the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Study #6 — Enhancing the Profession
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion key on Enhancing the Profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses responsibilities to elevate professional standards, mentoring, and conduct that improves the reputation and practice of public relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Chapter Ethics Programs 2002 Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A document describing best practices for PRSA chapter ethics programs (2002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendations and sample materials for chapters to run local ethics education, adjudication, or advisory activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Chapter Ethics Programs 2003 Best Practices and Samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated best practices and sample materials for chapter-level ethics programs (2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes templates, sample procedures, and suggested program elements chapters can adopt to foster ethics awareness and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Report Questionable Ethical Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance titled 'How to Report Questionable Ethical Performance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-by-step instructions and contact points for reporting suspected ethical violations, including expectations for evidence and confidentiality considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Leadership: Ingredients of Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: A resource/document titled 'Ethics and Leadership: Ingredients of Excellence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores the relationship between ethical leadership and professional excellence; useful for training leaders on integrating ethics into organizational culture.
